items.text: A builder operates as a sole proprietorship. A judgment against the business exceeds business assets. What is the owner's exposure?
C. Unlimited personal liability - personal assets are reachable — A sole proprietorship provides no liability shield - the owner has unlimited personal liability (corpus 04 §1 entity table).
Two builders form a general partnership. One partner signs a supply contract the business cannot pay. What is the other partner's liability?
A. Unlimited joint and several liability for the partnership debt — In a general partnership each partner has unlimited joint and several liability for partnership debts (corpus 04 §1 entity table).
How does a Michigan builder's corporation obtain S-corporation status?

D. By filing a federal IRS election on Form 2553 — S-corporation status is a federal IRS election made on Form 2553, not a Michigan filing; Michigan follows the federal election (corpus 04 §1 and trap list).
Which business entity is subject to double taxation - tax at the entity level and again on shareholder dividends?
B. C-corporation — A C-corporation pays corporate income tax and shareholders pay tax again on dividends; S-corps, partnerships, and default LLCs are pass-through (corpus 04 §1 entity table).
What document is filed with LARA to form a Michigan LLC?
A. Articles of Organization — An LLC is formed by filing Articles of Organization with LARA; Articles of Incorporation form a corporation (corpus 04 §1 entity table).
Under accrual-basis accounting, when is income recorded?

C. When it is earned, and expenses when incurred — Accrual accounting records income when earned (billed) and expenses when incurred, which matches revenue to cost for accurate job costing (corpus 04 §2).
Which long-term contract accounting method recognizes revenue as the work progresses, usually on a cost-to-cost basis?
B. Percentage-of-completion method — Percentage-of-completion recognizes revenue as work progresses, usually cost-to-cost; completed-contract recognizes everything at completion (corpus 04 §2).
Which statement about the balance sheet is correct?

D. It is a snapshot at a point in time where assets equal liabilities plus owner's equity — The balance sheet is a point-in-time snapshot built on Assets = Liabilities + Owner's Equity; profit over a period is shown on the income statement (corpus 04 §2 and trap list).
A contractor has current assets of $180,000 and current liabilities of $90,000. What is the current ratio?
A. 2.0 — Current ratio = current assets divided by current liabilities: $180,000 / $90,000 = 2.0, a liquidity measure (corpus 04 §2).
A contractor has performed $250,000 of work on a job but has only billed $200,000. What is this condition called?
C. Underbilling - the contractor is financing the owner — Underbilling means work performed exceeds billings - the contractor is financing the owner, which is a cash-flow danger sign (corpus 04 §2).
A company has $120,000 of annual overhead and $600,000 of annual direct costs. What is its overhead rate?
D. 20 percent — Overhead rate = annual overhead divided by annual direct costs: $120,000 / $600,000 = 20 percent (corpus 04 §2 job costing).
A contractor has fixed overhead of $150,000 per year and works at a 30 percent gross margin. What annual revenue does he need to break even?
B. $500,000 — Break-even revenue = fixed overhead divided by gross margin percent: $150,000 / 0.30 = $500,000 (corpus 04 §2).
A contractor applies a 25 percent markup on cost. What gross profit margin does that produce on the selling price?
C. 20 percent — Margin = markup divided by (1 + markup): 0.25 / 1.25 = 20 percent (corpus 04 §2 markup-vs-margin table).
How many board feet are in a two-by-six that is 12 feet long?
A. 12 board feet — Board feet = nominal thickness x width x length in feet, divided by 12: (2 x 6 x 12) / 12 = 12 board feet (corpus 04 §3).
A 4-inch slab measures 20 feet by 30 feet. Approximately how many cubic yards of concrete does the pour require before waste?
B. 7.41 cubic yards — 20 x 30 x (4/12 ft) = 200 cubic feet; divided by 27 = 7.41 cubic yards - order about 8 with waste (corpus 04 §3 worked example).
A roof measures 3,000 square feet. How many roofing squares is that, before waste?
D. 30 squares — One roofing square = 100 square feet, so 3,000 SF / 100 = 30 squares; shingle waste factors run about 10-15 percent (corpus 04 §3).
Where does contingency belong in a remodeling estimate?

C. Applied before markup and profit, as a risk reserve of roughly 10 to 20 percent on remodels — Contingency is a risk reserve applied before profit - roughly 5-10 percent on new construction and 10-20 percent on remodels; treating it as profit is a listed trap (corpus 04 §3).
A contract includes $5,000 for bathroom fixtures the owner has not yet selected. What is this figure called, and what happens if actual cost differs?

A. An allowance - the owner pays or is credited the difference by change order — An allowance is a plug number for unselected items; the owner pays or is credited the difference by change order (corpus 04 §3).
In critical path method scheduling, how much float do tasks on the critical path have?
D. Zero float — The critical path is the longest chain of dependent tasks and sets the minimum project duration; critical tasks have zero float (corpus 04 §4).
Which surety bond guarantees that subcontractors and suppliers get paid?
B. Payment bond — The payment bond pays subs and suppliers; the performance bond guarantees completion of the work - confusing the two is a listed trap (corpus 04 §4).
A builder receives a draw check and is asked to sign a lien waiver before the check clears. Which waiver should he sign?

A. A conditional waiver, effective only when payment actually clears — A conditional waiver takes effect only when payment clears; an unconditional waiver is effective immediately, paid or not, so it should be signed only after funds clear (corpus 04 §2 and trap list).
What document breaks the contract price into line items and serves as the basis for progress billing?

D. The schedule of values — The schedule of values breaks the contract price into line items and is the basis for progress billing, as with the AIA G702 application and G703 continuation sheet (corpus 04 §2).
What total percentage of wages does an employer pay in matching FICA taxes?
B. 7.65 percent — The employer matches 6.2 percent Social Security plus 1.45 percent Medicare = 7.65 percent; 15.3 percent is the combined employer-plus-employee total (corpus 04 §5).
FUTA tax applies to how much of each employee's annual wages, and at what net rate with the full state credit?
C. First $7,000 at a net 0.6 percent — FUTA is 6.0 percent on the first $7,000 of wages per employee, reduced to a net 0.6 percent with the full state credit (corpus 04 §5).
A struggling contractor uses withheld employee income tax and FICA to make payroll instead of remitting it to the IRS. What is his personal exposure?

A. Owners and officers are personally liable for these trust fund taxes under the Trust Fund Recovery Penalty — Withheld income tax and FICA are trust fund taxes; owners and officers are personally liable under the Trust Fund Recovery Penalty if they are not remitted (corpus 04 §5).
For 2025-2026, what is the Michigan UIA taxable wage base for a qualified employer with all reports filed and no unpaid balance?

B. $9,000, reduced from the $9,500 statutory default — The statutory default wage base is $9,500, reduced to $9,000 for qualified employers while the UIA Trust Fund stays over $2.5 billion - the $9,000 base applies in 2025-2026 (corpus 04 §5, MI UIA).
In 2026, a builder pays an independent contractor $1,500 for the year. Must he issue a 1099-NEC?

D. No - the reporting threshold for payments made after December 31, 2025 is $2,000 — PL 119-21 §70433 raised the 1099-NEC reporting threshold from $600 to $2,000 for payments made after December 31, 2025, so a $1,500 payment in 2026 falls below it; older materials still say $600 (corpus 04 §5).
A builder has only 1 employee, who has worked 40 hours per week for the past 6 months. Is Michigan workers' compensation coverage required?

C. Yes - one employee regularly employed 35 or more hours per week for 13 weeks or longer in the preceding 52 weeks triggers coverage — MCL 418.115(b) independently requires coverage when at least 1 employee has been regularly employed 35+ hours per week for 13 weeks or longer during the preceding 52 weeks; the 3-employee rule in 418.115(a) is a separate trigger.
A GC hires a sub who carries no workers' comp coverage and has no valid exclusion. The sub's employee is injured on the job. Who can the claim land on?

B. The general contractor, under statutory-principal liability — Under MCL 418.171, if a sub has no WC coverage and no valid exclusion, the injured worker's claim can land on the general contractor as statutory principal - always collect a WC certificate or WC-337 first (corpus 04 §6).
A jobsite fatality occurs Friday afternoon. Within what time must the employer report it to MIOSHA?
D. 8 hours — A work-related fatality must be reported to MIOSHA within 8 hours; in-patient hospitalization, amputation, or loss of an eye must be reported within 24 hours (corpus 04 §5).
